## Purpose and Entry Points
PHPWord is a Composer-installed PHP library for constructing, reading, templating, and serializing office documents. Its public object-model entry point is `src/PhpWord/PhpWord.php`; format selection and reader/writer creation are centralized in `src/PhpWord/IOFactory.php`. Consumers create a document, add a section and nested elements, then save through a writer or load through a reader.

## Canonical Document Model
`PhpWord` owns document-wide metadata, settings, styles, media, and sections. A section is the required top-level content container; containers recursively hold document elements such as text runs, tables, headers/footers, charts, notes, and fields.
- `src/PhpWord/PhpWord.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Element/Section.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Element/AbstractContainer.php`

The model is format-neutral: readers populate it and writers consume it. This is the central boundary separating authoring semantics from file-format syntax.

## Elements, Styles, and Cross-References
Elements carry content and local formatting, while reusable named and inline styles are represented separately. Shared collections track features requiring document-global IDs or auxiliary parts—footnotes, endnotes, comments, bookmarks, charts, and titles.
- `src/PhpWord/Element/AbstractElement.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Style.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Collection/Footnotes.php`

Changes to an element often require corresponding writer support across each target format and potentially relationship/part generation for OOXML or ODF.

## Reader Pipeline
`IOFactory` dispatches source files to reader implementations for Word 2007/OOXML, ODT, RTF, legacy `.doc`, and HTML. Readers parse format-specific package parts or streams and translate them into the canonical model. OOXML reading is partitioned by document, style, numbering, metadata, comment, and note parts.
- `src/PhpWord/Reader/AbstractReader.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Reader/Word2007.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Reader/Word2007/Document.php`

Reader support is asymmetric by format; unsupported source features may not survive model conversion or later serialization.

## Writer and Packaging Pipeline
Writers traverse the canonical model and emit Word2007/DOCX, ODT, RTF, HTML, EPUB3, or PDF. Each writer has format-specific element and style serializers; package-oriented formats additionally assemble required parts, manifests/content types, relationships, metadata, media, and ZIP output.
- `src/PhpWord/Writer/AbstractWriter.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Writer/Word2007.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Writer/Word2007/Part/Document.php`

PDF is an adapter boundary: it renders through configured Dompdf, mPDF, or TCPDF implementations rather than being a native layout engine.
- `src/PhpWord/Writer/PDF/AbstractRenderer.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Writer/PDF/DomPDF.php`

## Template Processing
`TemplateProcessor` operates directly on OOXML template packages for macro replacement, block/row cloning, image/chart substitution, and XSL transforms. It is a parallel generation route rather than normal construction through the element graph.
- `src/PhpWord/TemplateProcessor.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Shared/ZipArchive.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Shared/XMLWriter.php`

## Runtime, Dependencies, and Delivery
Runtime is PHP 7.1+ with Composer (`composer.json`). XML parser/XMLWriter, ZIP, GD, and XSL extensions enable key format, image, and template capabilities; Laminas Escaper is required and PDF renderer libraries are optional. Package/XML and image handling are encapsulated in shared infrastructure.
- `src/PhpWord/Settings.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Shared/ZipArchive.php`
- `src/PhpWord/Shared/Drawing.php`

CI validates the library via GitHub Actions; documentation deployment is defined separately.
- `.github/workflows/php.yml`
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
